set_text.text: Markup is the amount you add to a cost to set a price, written as a share of that cost. It is a rule for reaching a price, not the share of the price you keep.
What you paid, not what you charge. Because the base is the cost, a markup can run past 100%, while a margin never reaches it.
Markup on cost, markup on retail
Distributors usually state markup on cost. Retail pricing often states it on the selling price instead, so a store buyer's 40% may already be a margin.
Why the trade keeps using it
It is one multiplication on a number you already know. Cost times 1.40 prices a $22.00 case at $30.80 on the spot. Hitting a margin takes a division instead.
Who uses a product markup calculator
It is built for independent food distributors who price off a cost sheet. Anyone who sets a markup, translates a buyer's percentage or checks a price list should run it.
